source.title: Grokking as Structural Inference: Transformers Need Bayesian Lottery Tickets
source.authors: K. Hidajat; Solden Stoll; J. An

record.tranche_reason: The study tests delayed generalization and a proposed mechanism on algorithmic sequence tasks, using attention-alignment and norm measurements rather than reproducing the original studies' full recipe.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on modular addition and additional algorithmic tasks, including train/test trajectories, attention alignment, and norm/structure interventions. The Bayesian-ticket versus lottery-ticket comparison is omitted as a comparison of the study's proposed method; the text does not report identifiable algorithms across runs or a training-set-size sweep.
record.test_reason: The study trains a one-layer Transformer on modular addition (p=113, train fraction 0.3) and reports baseline train/test trajectories showing delayed generalization (V1). It tracks attention divergence from the oracle as a continuous progress measure that collapses before test accuracy rises (V2). It also runs a weight-decay/norm × attention-routing factorial bearing on the low-norm account (V5). This is a different method aimed at the same question, with no replication of either original recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that generalization in attention models requires both an MLP Goldilocks norm condition and attention mass on every informative token. They attribute the delay to post-memorization gradient starvation that weight decay must erode, and argue a KL structural prior bypasses the wait with a 1/β scaling. They also claim this 'Bayesian ticket' matches or beats lottery-ticket transfer. They acknowledge that sufficiency depends on the Decoupled Max-Margin Assumption and that the analysis assumes a single-layer, single-head, fixed-query architecture.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a minimal single-layer, single-head Transformer with a two-layer ReLU MLP, tracks attention structure and MLP norm, and adds norm-matching and KL-prior interventions; it is not described as an explicit replication of either original source.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported transition differs by task: modular addition is the cleanest, while sparse parity and permutation composition are noisier or faster. KL penalty strength changes the grokking epoch. The study also reports a structural bypass when informative positions vary by example.

fits_no_version.finding: After memorization, the attention task-gradient norm collapses by orders of magnitude and stays below the derived Pinsker bound (gradient starvation / explaining away).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Delayed grokking in Transformers reflects starvation of the attention gradient once the MLP has memorized the training set.

fits_no_version.finding: A KL penalty toward oracle attention advances the grokking epoch roughly linearly in 1/β, and a sequence-dependent oracle prior bypasses the plateau.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Direct attention supervision toward informative tokens removes the grokking delay.

record.problems: The main experiments are on algorithmic sequence tasks, principally modular addition. Curves are averaged over 5 seeds unless otherwise stated, but no error bars or other uncertainty measures are reported. The study does not vary training-set size. The theoretical sufficiency direction depends on the Decoupled Max-Margin Assumption, and the architecture is restricted.
record.rows_left_out: The Bayesian-ticket versus lottery-ticket comparison in Figure 4 is omitted because it compares the study's proposed method with another method rather than directly measuring a claim version. Related appendix plots are omitted where they report distractor-length robustness, embedding-dimension effects, or optimizer norm decay without directly measuring the delayed-generalization behavior named by the versions.

untested.parts: Dependence of the delay on training-set size: the train fraction is fixed at 0.3.
Fourier/circuit identification and the removal of identified memorizing components. The progress measure used is attention KL to an oracle, not a circuit-level measure.
Circuit efficiency comparison, critical dataset size, and ungrokking below it. No weight-decay strength sweep is reported, only theoretical 1/λ derivation.
Not tested: no non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale manipulation.
Not tested: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Not tested: no comparison of learned algorithms across runs.
Not tested. Optimizer variants (batch size, Adam betas) are measured only on MLP norm decay, not on grokking delay; there is no softmax floating-point test.

missing.what: Baseline WD vs No-WD trajectories in the factorial: whether the baseline model groks without weight decay. This bears directly on V5 but the text does not describe it.
missing.locator: Figure 2 (Baseline panel, WD/NM/No WD legend); Appendix G.3

missing.what: Freezing attention to oracle routing makes the MLP generalize far earlier than the coupled baseline.
Approximate grokking epochs from the β sweep (plot range about 1500–3500) and the baseline grokking epoch.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is mostly qualitative text and figures; no numerical accuracies or uncertainty bands are given in the text. The authors' theory says structural learning halts during the plateau, which sits in some tension with V2's 'gradual formation', but the measured KL still precedes the test jump. The adversarial-prior condition is induced by construction. The KL and oracle-prior results are the study's own method and are treated as not bearing on the versions. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not vary training-set size or test whether smaller training sets require more optimization.
It measures attention alignment and MLP norm, not a Fourier algorithm or the removal of identified memorizing circuit components.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition test.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
The study tests norm and structural conditions, but not circuit efficiency, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
No identification or comparison of the algorithms learned across runs.

Optimizer perturbations are discussed, but the study does not test whether grokking delay disappears under controlled optimizer or numerical conditions; it does not test floating-point softmax limits.

rows.value: Remains near chance until structural divergence is small, then sharply transitions to 100%.

rows.subject: single-layer, single-head Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Track KL divergence between learned attention and oracle attention.
rows.value: The attention posterior condenses before test accuracy rises; test performance stays near chance until the divergence has largely collapsed.
rows.note: This is the study's continuous structural-progress measure; no exact divergence values are stated in the text.

rows.subject: single-layer, single-head Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Track the task-gradient norm with respect to attention parameters.
rows.measure: Frobenius norm of attention task gradient
rows.value: An initial spike during memorization is followed by a collapse to a tiny residual signal during the plateau.
rows.note: The authors describe the small post-memorization gradient as gradient starvation.
rows.check: Attention task-gradient norm is a diagnostic for the authors' gradient-starvation account. It does not measure gradual formation of a generalizing circuit or a progress measure anticipating the jump, so it should not be linked to V2. Moved to fits_no_version.

source_check.notes: §6 describes norm matching as projection of MLP weights onto an rmax shell, whereas Appendix G.3 specifies a WQ/WK L2 penalty with qk_penalty=0.5; the implemented intervention is unresolved. The separate transition-holdout experiment is outside this study.

statements.correction: This study: modular addition modulo 113; adversarial routing with norm matching leaves test accuracy at chance; oracle routing without norm control gives partial generalization; capacity control with structural routing gives perfect generalization.
statements.problem: The modular-addition findings are accurately summarized. The separately described transition-holdout experiment and its numerical results are not reported in this study and cannot be verified against it.
